setlist.title: Stuck Inside of Mobile with the Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): First set was relatively strong, peaking with an above-average Bird Song [17][18]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Jerry skipped his solo in the middle of Stella Blue; second set considered weak [17][18]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Jerry brought out a strong Wheel after Space, which led straight into I Need A Miracle [12]
- **I Need A Miracle** (1 review): Vince and Bruce swapped keyboard positions for Miracle; audible if you listen closely [14]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Jerry rebounded with Sugaree after the unlisted Picasso Moon that followed The Weight [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mystery**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd91-08-12.sbd.fishman.8109.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 217 min; rated 2.88/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Cassette hiss is present; the mix evens out by Minglewood, with Phil's bass very strong. Beefy soundboard; Another copy of this recording sounds a bit cleaner; Reviewer calls the recording quality great [13][17][20][22]
- **gd1991-08-12.sbd.hinko.29496.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Another copy of this recording sounds a bit cleaner [18]
- **gd1991-08-12.fob.brennecke-young.GEMS.96371.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [4]
- **gd1991-08-12.akg451.darby.119081.flac16**: audience recording; 18 songs; 153 min [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; Cal Expo still allowed camping. Iko Iko was done in an unusual way [12]
- Reviewer's first out-of-town run and first with lights and visuals; flew to Sacramento and expected a huge stadium [16]
- Reviewer met his future wife through a friend before the show; they have been together nearly 17 years [19]
- Reviewer found Vince's keyboards intrusive, the setlist uninspired, and the band seemingly flubbing through [20]
- Opened a six-night run at Cal Expo and Shoreline, soon after Jerry left rehab again; show felt strange [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-08-12.sbd.fishman.8109.sbeok.shnf**: source: Don Pearson Master Cassette > Cassette > D > CD-r [1]. Also: Disc three uses filler from the 8-13-91 first set [1]
- **gd1991-08-12.sbd.hinko.29496.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: flac16 SBD > DAT > CD > EAC > FLAC [2]
- **gd1991-08-12.fob.brennecke-young.GEMS.96371.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: Schoeps Omni -> Oade Supply -> Panasonic SV-255 (Recording Location: FOB, on stands 8 feet hight and mic stands spaced 8.5 feet apart) [4]. Also: Reviewer once had a cassette master of this DAT from Keith Weiner of Los Gatos, CA; the crowd sounds familiar [21]
- **gd1991-08-12.akg451.darby.119081.flac16**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; AKGC451EB/CK1's (DIN/DFC/Middle Of OTS/6 Feet High)> Whirlwind Phantoms>Sony TC-D5M; Tapes TDK MA-X Set 1,Sony Metal E-S… [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Cal Expo Amphitheatre - August 13, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/august-13-1991) [25]
- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Cal Expo Amphitheater, Aug 12, 1991 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/CLX910812-A.html) [26]
